the mussel-dominated communities that are found along the East Pacific Rise are not the result of mussel competition with other species but are the result of a combination of factors that includes a high temperature regime, low levels of H2S/ HS− in the vent fluid, and low levels of seismic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the interrelationships between physical and chemical factors that control biological community structure in hydrothermal systems and how these relationships change over time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the biological communities in this mussel-dominated habitat are highly dynamic and respond to changes in the vent fluid chemistry and physical conditions, which are, in turn, influenced by volcanic activity.
the mussel-dominated community is a transient community that forms and persists in a vent field only until the underlying volcanic activity ceases.
the mussel bed was formed and maintained as a result of a complex interplay between vent fluid chemistry and the physical environment, including the effects of seismicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mussels are not the dominant species because they can not tolerate the high temperatures, but because they can tolerate the high temperatures they can be the first species to colonize the vents and they are the dominant species until the other organisms can colonize the area.

mussel-dominated communities are associated with high-temperature vent fluids that are relatively depleted in sulfide and that are characterized by high rates of microbial sulfide oxidation, whereas vestimentiferan-dominated communities are associated primarily with low-temperature vent fluids, which are relatively rich in sulfide and have relatively low rates of microbial sulfidic oxidation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
mussel-dominated hydrothermal vent habitats are not only highly productive but also highly dynamic.
the mussel bed at 9°50′N is highly resilient to perturbations and can rapidly recover from disturbances.
the mussels that dominate the vent fauna in this region have a much narrower thermal tolerance than the vestimentiferans.
